children: Andre Loranger has been appointed as Britain's next National Statistician, the U.K. Statistics Authority said Tuesday, overseeing the publication of national data that has faced criticism over its reliability.
Loranger, currently Chief Statistician of Canada, takes over from Ian Diamond, who resigned in May 2025 due to health issues.

Diamond's departure came shortly before the publication of a government review of the Office for National Statistics that criticized its management. The role of the U.K.'s top statistician was split last year, with a civil servant now serving as its permanent secretary.

The National Statistician role is the top adviser to the country's statistics authority and government on quality of official statistics. The ONS has in recent years faced challenges from lawmakers over its reliability, suspended its top labor-market survey, and temporarily delayed retail sales and producer-price data over quality issues.

Loranger will serve for a term of five years, taking up his position later this fall, the U.K. Statistics Authority said. His recruitment from Canada echoes the hiring of the then central-bank governor Mark Carney to lead the Bank of England in 2013. Carney is now Canada's prime minister.

"[Loranger's] deep experience in Canada and on the international stage will accelerate our work to unlock greater value across the U.K. statistical system for users, by increasing engagement and supporting a culture of openness and innovation," said Penny Young, interim chair of the U.K. Statistics Authority.
